title: She could get up on a truss of hay
html_source: This is a line in the first stanza of “The Low-Backed Car”. Other music references appearing in this paragraph are as follows: “Ballyhooly” is from an old Irish temperance song; “Colleen Bawn” is a symbol of Irish womanhood from The Lily of Killarney; “The Tune the Old Cow Died On” is a more comic song in which a farmer plays bagpipes to his cow, and the cow, in attempting to emulate the noise, expires.
